questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Courses, distance, culture, and the highlands.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: If it weren't for covid restrictions and industrial action at UoE 10/10.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It has been relatively easy. Otherwise, the office for international students was helpful and often replied within a day or two.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Changing courses, covid isolation, and postponing essays.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: As an international student, you'll get assigned to a personal tutor, which is convenient and helpful when you're new on campus.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Not easy. Two of my friends from KU and I tried finding an HMO licensed flat to rent close to UoE and the city centre. It was more complicated than we thought with letting agencies and we needed to have a guarantor. After three weeks, we found a 3 bedroom flat in Bruntsfield but with my dad's friend's help who lives in Edinburgh. It was definitely worth the fuss! Huge flat 15 minutes walk to UoE :D

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: If you want to rent a flat try and do it before your arrival. But it might be a lot easier if you just want to rent a room in a private student flat (off-campus).

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Go on Facebook and join student housing groups!

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I remember the process as straightforward and trouble-free.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You had to apply for courses, and then fill out a digital form.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I could contact the office for international students or my personal tutor.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: At first, I was quite gutted that I didn't get any film courses, but I ended up enjoying dipping my toes in the field of sociology and anthropology.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't worry if you don't get the courses you wanted, they might turn out to be interesting. And studying abroad is so much more than the academic opportunities ;)

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: If it weren't for covid restrictions and online lectures 4/5.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The courses available for international undergrad students are mostly with other 1st or 2nd-year students.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The lectures were quite similar to the ones at UCPH. However, having tutorials 3 times a week with 8-12 people discussing different topics and articles differs.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Ethics and Politics of Data 
Social Anthropology 1B: Anthropology Matters
Sociology 1B: The Sociological Imagination: Private Troubles, Public Problems

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend all of them!

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I didn't really join any non-academic activities.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There are a lot of student activities e.g. hiking, skiing, yoga, and book clubs.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I didn't join any sry.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: GO TO THE HIGHLANDS!! Isle of Skye, Inverness, Glencoe, and Pentland Hills, just to mention a few.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy. Scottish people are really chatty and outgoing.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Put yourself out there! And you don't have to find your friends on campus or at the events for the international students.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I didn't find any cultural differences challenging.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The Scottish banter and openmindedness.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Go explore Scotland, find private accommodation and don't worry about the amount of coursework.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: If you experience any challenges during your mobility contact your personal tutor.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: In general, Edinburgh is just an amazing city with a lot to offer.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: There is a difference in writing style, references etc. when it comes to written exams.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
